messages.author: 7a0c0a1d5af6ca55
messages.subject: sampling from the posterior of a fitted student-t regression model
parts:
If I have a model fitted with the Student t-family response, and want to draw samples of the response from the fitted model, is this the correct way to do, specifically for how the t response is parametrised in inla.doc("T"):

t_pp_draw <- function(inla_model, num_simulations) {
  # generate samples from the posterior
  samples <- inla.posterior.sample(n = num_simulations, result = inla_model)
 
  nu_loc <- grep("degrees of freedom for student-t", names(samples[[1]]$hyperpar))
  tau_loc <- grep("precision for the student-t observations", names(samples[[1]]$hyperpar))
 
  # the linear predictor
  eta <- inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", samples)
 
  # the degrees of freedom for the student t
  nu <- inla.hyperpar.sample(n = num_simulations, result = inla_model)[, nu_loc]
 
  # the precision parameter
  tau <- inla.hyperpar.sample(n = num_simulations, result = inla_model)[, tau_loc]
 
  yvals <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(eta), ncol = num_simulations)
  for (i in 1:num_simulations) {
    yvals[, i] <- as.numeric(eta[, i]) + (rt(nrow(eta), df = nu[i]) / sqrt(tau[i]))
  }
  return(yvals)
}


Code largely adapted from how inlatools::distribution_check() is styled

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] sampling from the posterior of a fitted student-t regression model
parts:
you need to evaluate the t-noise at the same level as the predictor as they are
dependent

n <- 100
x <- rnorm(n)
df <- 5
y <- 1 + x + rt(n, df = df)/sqrt(df/(df-2))

r <- inla(y ~ 1 + x,
family = "t",
data = data.frame(y, x),
control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

sim <- function(idx.prec, idx.df) {
n <- length(Predictor)
df <- theta[idx.df]
y <- Predictor + rt(n, df = df) / sqrt(df/(df-2))
return (y)
}

xx <- inla.posterior.sample(10^4, r, intern = FALSE)
yy <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(sim, xx,
## index for the precision and df parameter
idx.prec = 1, idx.df = 2)
